text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Incident 2061234567 — Multiple private-connect customers in azure-australiasoutheast reporting elevated request failures and asymmetric routing to on-prem. Auto-detect: VPN/ExpressRoute-type links showing route instability. Paging on-call SREs now.

SRE - Priya: Ack, I'm on it. Priya here. Can someone from NetOps pull current BGP state for the active VPN/EDGE gateways? Also which customers are impacted (brief)?

NetOps - Jules: pulling now. Quick summary from our telemetry: 2x gateways in australiasoutheast are showing frequent BGP withdraws to our onprem prefixes (10.8.0.0/16 + 10.9.0.0/16). Looks like one of MSFT aggregation nodes is flapping.

NetOps - Jules: paste of bgp neighbors and recent flaps:
```
# show ip bgp neighbors summary
Neighbor        AS   MsgRcv  MsgSent   TblVer  Up/Down  State
10.254.12.3     65515   12345    12342     2314     00:12:34  Idled
10.254.12.4     65515   23456    23450     2314     00:00:10  Active(restart)

# tail /var/log/bgp-daemon.log
2026-03-15T01:12:04Z BGP: received withdraw for 10.8.0.0/16
2026-03-15T01:12:11Z BGP: received withdraw for 10.9.0.0/16
2026-03-15T01:12:19Z BGP: neighbor 10.254.12.4 reset (TCP reset)
```

SRE - Priya: ok that aligns with user reports. CS, any enterprise customers on Private in AUS we should notify now?

CS - Maria: AcmeHealth (private deployment, AUS) reported a spike of 502s starting ~01:10 UTC and seeing POSTs to our inference endpoint time out. Their ops forwarded an example trace: 
`POST /v1/predict 502 at 01:11:03, RTT 1200ms`
They're escalated to SEV and want ETA.

Support - Tom: I put the customer on a temporary status page update and told them we're investigating network routes and will follow up.

Eng - Ivan: Two quick mitigations we can do from the platform side: 1) trigger smart-routing fallback for private customers in that region to australiaeast, 2) spin up a short-lived dedicated path that terminates in a stable region and announce routes via our DR peering. I can run the API call to flip routing for AcmeHealth only.

SRE - Priya: Do it for AcmeHealth and any customers with active onprem connections in AUS. Use canary first (10% traffic), watch errors for 10m, then enlarge. Post the API call here.

Eng - Ivan: calling the routing API now:
```bash
# curl -X POST https://console.redwood.ai/api/routing/fallback 
# body: {"scope":"customers","ids":["acmehealth"],"from_region":"azure-australiasoutheast","to_region":"azure-australiaeast","percent":10}
```
Response: 202 Accepted. Job id: fbk-9a3f

incident-bot: Automated update: job fbk-9a3f started, preview routes pushed to network edge.

NetOps - Jules: Microsoft side shows partial reconvergence but still intermittent TCP RSTs to our peer IPs. I've opened an azure support case — ticket MSFT-987654. Requesting BGP neighbor pcap and timestamps.

azure-support-bot: Case MSFT-987654 created, initial triage indicated: "possible aggregation node instability affecting VPN tunnels and BGP sessions". Engaged on-call network team at Microsoft.

SRE - Priya: Good. Monitoring metrics — error rate for Private customers in AUS dropped from 18% -> 12% after 10% fallback. Continue to increase if stable.

Eng - Ivan: Increasing fallback to 50% for acmehealth + 3 other private tenants. API job fbk-9a3f updated -> percent:50.

incident-bot: Update: fbk-9a3f progress 50% routes applied.

CS - Maria: AcmeHealth confirms reduced errors but still seeing high latencies on some requests (>800ms). They're requesting a timeline.

SRE - Priya: Temp mitigation status: partial traffic reroute to australiaeast is reducing failures; however the underlying BGP flaps on azure side remain and could re-introduce issues. Next steps: 1) Collect packet captures from our VPN edge for MSFT case, 2) ask MSFT for fix ETA, 3) keep fallbacks in place until stable, 4) prepare customer comms w/ remediation steps and expected next update in 30m.

Support - Tom: Draft status blurb for customers: 
"We’re investigating routing instability affecting private connections in azure-australiasoutheast. We’ve enabled partial routing fallback to australiaeast for impacted private tenants which has reduced failures. Azure support engaged. Next update 30 minutes."

SRE - Priya: I'm going to escalate to P1 internal if MSFT can't provide ETA in 20m. For now continuing monitoring. Paging night SRE for handoff in 45m: Aaron, FYI you'll be taking this at the 02:00 UTC rotation — summarize below.

SRE - Aaron: Acknowledged. I'll handle the overnight handoff. Please drop final runbook link.

NetOps - Jules: uploaded captures + bgp logs to case MSFT-987654 and our internal S3: s3://redwood-ops/incidents/2061234567/. Also adding packetfilter pcap snippet for 01:10-01:20 UTC.

SRE - Priya: Final quick notes for handoff -> Aaron:
- Impact: Private/on-prem connected tenants in azure-australiasoutheast experiencing intermittent route withdraws causing 5xx and high latency to inference endpoints.
- Mitigations in place: Smart-routing fallback partial -> australiaeast (50% for affected customers), active monitoring, azure case opened MSFT-987654.
- Next actions: coordinate with MSFT on fix/ETA, consider full cutover to australiaeast if flaps persist >1h, consider rolling Dedicated for largest tenant (AcmeHealth) if they request guaranteed capacity.
- Links: S3 logs link, routing job fbk-9a3f, internal runbook https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/azure-bgp-flap (oncall creds required).

SRE - Aaron: Got it. I'll take over per rotation. If MSFT provides fix, revert fallbacks only after 3x stable 10-minute windows and announce to customers.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident 2061234567 updated. Next update scheduled in 30 minutes or on-EScalation.

SRE - Priya: Thanks everyone. Leaving thread; ping me if MSFT gives an ETA under 15m.

CS - Maria: I'll send an interim email to AcmeHealth summarizing the above and tell them Aaron will be the point overnight.

Support - Tom: Marking incident as active in status dashboard.

(End of thread)
